title: Gate-crashing Bobby Kennedy's funeral at St. Patrick's
place_text: St. Patrick's Cathedral, New York City

tellings.quote: walks up to us and he says, "Russian Orthodox representatives?" And I say, "No, Sloanic Orthodox representatives."

plain: The writer Peter Levenda, billed on the show as a historian, says that in 1968 he and a companion slipped uninvited into Bobby Kennedy's funeral at St. Patrick's Cathedral in New York. When an official walked up and asked if they were "Russian Orthodox representatives," Levenda says he answered that no, they represented a different Orthodox church, and they got in among mourners such as Rose Kennedy and Jackie Onassis. He tells it as his own story and says a still photograph of the funeral procession shows it.
